images.title: A strip that does not fit
images.purpose: Show that a strip with a shorter top and a longer bottom does not land on its old outline after a half turn.
images.composition: Two shapes side by side with wide space between: the strip in its start position on the left, the half turned strip on the right over a dotted outline.
images.exact_structure: Left: one teal #0072B2 four sided strip with a 2 cm top, a 4 cm bottom and two equal slanting sides, a centre dot, and a reddish purple #CC79A7 tick on the short top side. Right: the same strip turned 180 degrees about its dot in amber #E69F00, over a dotted grey #6B7280 copy of the old outline; the tick is now at the bottom, the longer side is on top, and the shapes visibly do not match. Exactly 2 strips and 1 dotted outline.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
a strip whose slanting sides are unequal, or a half turned strip that matches the old outline
images.takeaway: A turn counts only if the strip lands exactly on its old outline.
images.description: A teal strip with a 2 cm top and 4 cm bottom, and the same strip turned 180 degrees in amber over a dotted old outline, clearly not matching.
images.context: Shown with the concept as its one key picture, next to the walkthrough video. PLACEHOLDER: specified, not generated yet.
images.teaching_notes: Ask the student to point at the top side before and after the turn and say why the outline does not match.

image_decisions.why: The half turn test on the strip is a picture idea; one clean image carries it.
